scorecard.rationale: A small essential-oil massage comparison reported defecation benefit but left methods and counts incompletely specified. The rosemary-extract trial has no posted results and tracks a combined bowel adverse-event question. The ground rosemary Parkinson constipation effect remains unresolved. The rosemary extract preprint reports more wet stools at lower oral levels in otherwise unchallenged mice, and slower transit at higher injected levels in a separate induced-diarrhea model. Neither procedure identifies which effect, if either, transfers to ground rosemary intake. The human oil-massage design does not isolate rosemary, and the registered extract trial still has no posted results.
